\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{गुल्फः} (gulphaḥ)}{गुल्फः (gulphaḥ)}]{\sk{गुल्फः} (gulphaḥ) — an ankle}

\label{lesson:SA-C118-gulphah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for an eyebrow, then the Sanskrit for the skin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{गुल्फः}}
\textbf{\sk{गुल्फः}} — \emph{gulphaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}an ankle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gulpha} \textquotedblleft{}the ankle\textquotedblright{}, also \emph{kulpha} in the Rigveda, is perhaps borrowed from Dravidian: CDIAL 4216, after Burrow, takes the wavering \emph{k-} and \emph{g-} as a sign of that and compares a Dravidian word for \textquotedblleft{}hoof\textquotedblright{}. It lives on as Marathi \emph{gophā} \textquotedblleft{}ankle\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4216).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gulphaḥ}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Sanskrit for an eyebrow, then the Sanskrit for the skin, then say \emph{gulphaḥ} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{अंगुलिः} (aṅguliḥ)}{अंगुलिः (aṅguliḥ)}]{\sk{अंगुलिः} (aṅguliḥ) — a finger}

\label{lesson:SA-C118-angulih}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for the skin, then the Sanskrit for an ankle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{अंगुलिः}}
\textbf{\sk{अंगुलिः}} — \emph{aṅguliḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a finger\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{aṅguli} \textquotedblleft{}a finger, a toe\textquotedblright{} is built on the base \emph{aṅgu-}, the same base as \emph{aṅguṣṭha} \textquotedblleft{}thumb\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 135, 137). It lives on as Hindi \emph{uṅglī} \textquotedblleft{}finger\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 135).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{कक्षः} (kakṣaḥ)}{कक्षः (kakṣaḥ)}]{\sk{कक्षः} (kakṣaḥ) — a room}

\label{lesson:SA-C118-kaksah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for an ankle, then the Sanskrit for a finger.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{कक्षः}}
\textbf{\sk{कक्षः}} — \emph{kakṣaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a room\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kakṣa} first meant \textquotedblleft{}a hiding place\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}the armpit\textquotedblright{}, which MW calls the most concealed part of the body; its feminine \emph{kakṣā} also names a walled enclosure or a private room. MW compares Latin \emph{coxa} \textquotedblleft{}hip\textquotedblright{}, and EtymDB counts it as inherited from Indo-European.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{आसन्दी} (āsandī)}{आसन्दी (āsandī)}]{\sk{आसन्दी} (āsandī) — a chair}

\label{lesson:SA-C118-asandi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a finger, then the Sanskrit for a room.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{आसन्दी}}
\textbf{\sk{आसन्दी}} — \emph{āsandī} — \textquotedblleft{}a chair\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{āsandī} \textquotedblleft{}a chair, a stool\textquotedblright{} is old, in the Atharvaveda, and comes from \emph{ā} \textquotedblleft{}on\textquotedblright{} + the root √sad \textquotedblleft{}sit\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 1485). MW sets √sad beside Latin \emph{sedere} and English \emph{sit}: an inherited Indo-European root.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{फलकम्} (phalakam)}{फलकम् (phalakam)}]{\sk{फलकम्} (phalakam) — a board, a plank}

\label{lesson:SA-C118-phalakam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a room, then the Sanskrit for a chair.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{फलकम्}}
\textbf{\sk{फलकम्}} — \emph{phalakam} — \textquotedblleft{}a board, a plank\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{phalaka} \textquotedblleft{}a board, a plank, a bench\textquotedblright{} is found from the Brāhmaṇas on (MW). CDIAL 9053 refers it to the root √phal \textquotedblleft{}burst, split\textquotedblright{}, the root MW files it under, and MW compares √phal with English \emph{split}. Nepali kept it as \emph{phalek} \textquotedblleft{}board, plank\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9053).
\end{cousinweb}
